header: of carbon dioxide the heat network did not emit in 2026
bodytext:
The figure is a comparison, not a measurement. Nothing was weighed: what we know is how much heat left the network, and what that heat would have cost in emissions if each of those 9,400 flats had burned gas in its own boiler instead. The difference is 41,200 tonnes.

That makes the reference case the whole argument. We use individual condensing boilers at the efficiency the national environment agency publishes, because that is what most of these buildings had before they were connected. Against a fleet of new heat pumps the saving would be far smaller, and against the coal boilers of 1990 it would be far larger.
note: Emission factors: national environment agency, 2026 edition. Heat delivered: 214 GWh, metered at the building substations. Reference case: individual gas condensing boilers at 92 % annual efficiency. Calculated by our controlling team in February 2027.
